resources.string:
A clone is another copy of an app, installed beside it. Each copy has its own name, package, and data. The original app stays installed and unchanged.

You can make more than one clone of the same app. A clone starts empty: you sign in again inside that copy.

Some apps look up their own package name and refuse to run. Banking apps, and some messengers and games, do this. Clone Space does not try to hide the new name from the app.
Android installs each clone the way it installs any other app. Turn on Allow from this source for Clone Space. You only need to do this once.
%1$s and its data will be deleted. The original app stays installed.
